editorial:
Imagine leaning back in your favorite chair and letting your mind drift away with some great music. That is exactly what you get here. You are treated to a wild mix of sounds and sights that feel more like a dream than a standard movie. It blends cool shots of American landscapes and the strange, empty streets of Venice with bright computer graphics and views of deep space. You will also see the band performing live and traveling around, giving you a real peek into their world. It feels like a digital art gallery that you can just sink into without any stress.

What really works is how the music drives the whole experience, making the slow pace feel relaxing rather than boring. The visuals are a bit dated since it came out in 1997, but that actually gives it a nostalgic, retro charm that is pretty cool. If you love electronic music or just need something to chill out to, you should definitely check this out. It is best enjoyed streaming in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to see those space colors pop, or you can add the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection for the best sound quality.
endingExplained: The film wraps up by blending all its different themes together into one final sequence. You see the music build up as the images shift from the real world of Venice and the US to the imaginary world of outer space. It ends with a fade-out that leaves you feeling peaceful. There is no big plot twist because it is a visual journey, but it concludes by showing that music and art can take you anywhere.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves electronic music and ambient art.
